title: Federal Government Airlifts Additional Troops to Baidoa Amid Growing Threat from Laftagareen Loyalists
detail: Somalia's federal government airlifted additional troops into Baidoa on or around August 29, 2026 to protect South West State leader Sheikh Aadan Mohamed Nur Madobe and government facilities, citing a persistent threat from fighters loyal to former Southwest State president Laftagareen following the August 17 VBIED assault on the city. Garowe Online reported the reinforcement came as the AU has authorized AUSSOM to fight Al-Shabaab while barring it from taking sides in the Baidoa political standoff (see Aug 28 memo), leaving the federal government to rely on its own SNA units to secure South West State's capital. Unit numbers and composition were not disclosed.

media.caption: Federal forces reinforced Baidoa amid a persistent threat from Laftagareen-aligned fighters, reported Aug 29, 2026

title: Turkish Cargo Ship MV Lutuf Freed After 12 Days — Somalia Claims Military Rescue, Puntland Alleges Ransom Was Paid
detail: The Cameroon-flagged, Turkish-operated general cargo vessel MV Lutuf — hijacked by eight armed men on August 17, 2026 roughly four nautical miles off Mareeyo in Puntland's Eyl district while carrying Turkish military supplies, communications equipment and satellite gear from the Port of Tekirdag bound for the TURKSOM base in Mogadishu, with 10 crew aboard (6 Indian, 1 Turkish, 1 Georgian, 2 Serbian security personnel) — was released around August 29-30, 2026 after 12 days in pirate hands. Somalia's Ministry of Defence said Turkish naval forces and the Somali armed forces conducted a 10-day joint operation that destroyed four pirate skiffs and killed 14 suspected pirates, with sustained pressure ultimately forcing the remaining hijackers to abandon the vessel; the ship resumed its voyage toward Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. Puntland's Ministry of Security disputed this account, saying 'there was no operation by the Federal Government of Somalia and/or Türkiye that rescued the vessel' and alleging a ransom of roughly $2-2.5 million was paid, facilitated by federal officials who had been in phone contact with the pirates since the hijacking. The dispute is the latest flashpoint between Mogadishu and Puntland over control of and credit for counter-piracy operations along the Puntland coast, and adds a new tactical detail to the 2026 piracy resurgence: the previously hijacked vessel Sward was reportedly used as a 'mothership' in the boarding of Lutuf.

media.caption: MV Lutuf was freed after 12 days in pirate hands off Puntland; Mogadishu and Puntland dispute whether it was a military rescue or a paid ransom
